 Order

This is the first Criminal Appeal filed by the appellant under Section 14-A(2) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 seeking anticipatory bail in connection with Crime No.222/2024 for offences punishable under Section 376 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(w)(i)(ii) and 3(2)(v) of SC & ST Act, 1989 registered at Police Station-Kevlari, District-Seoni (M.P.).
2.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the false case has been registered against the appellant.

On 27.03.2024, he was kidnapped on the instance of the complainant and Rs.1,00,000/-
was demanded.
He called his brother-in-law and his brother-in-law had arranged the money and given to kidnappers. After that, he was released and the victim of this case has been arrayed as a accused in this case.
She was actively involved in the kidnapping.
After knowing this fact, the FIR was lodged.
She had lodged this NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:5655 2 CRA-13736-2024 FIR.
The appellant is a reputed person and he has no criminal background.
To blackmail her and to make compromise in the case of kidnapping, this FIR was lodged.
Hence, he prayed that the appellant be given the benefit of anticipatory bail.

3. Learned counsel for the objector has submitted that the appellant is not entitled for the benefit of anticipatory bail as the case registered under the relevant Sections of SC & ST (POA) Act, 1989.
As per provision of Section 18-A(2) of SC & ST (POA) Act, 1989, the anticipatory bail is not maintainable.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the objector has further submitted that the appellant was harassing the victim and he is a influential person.
The incident happened on 27.03.2024.
On that date, he had violated her privacy.

When she told the story to his brother-in-law (Dever) and the family members,
the appellant had lodged the false report.
Due to his influence, the Police had not registered the FIR.

Though, she had given the written complaint against the appellant and that was received by Anusuchit Jati Janjati Kalyan Police Station, Seoni on 06.04.2024 and the matter was registered after she approached to Superintendent of Police and in the direction of Superintendent of Police,
Seoni,

entities.text: Anusuchit Jati Janjati Kalyan Police Station, Seoni
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: In the false case, the appellant had made her to be sent to the Jail.
Hence, no case of anticipatory bail is made out.

5. Learned counsel for the State has submitted that the case was registered but the statements of the appellant were recorded on 24.04.2024 and his statements under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. were also registered.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:5655 3 CRA-13736-2024 7.

Looking to the severity of the offence and provisions of Section 18- A(2) of SC & ST (POA) Act,
1989, this Court is not inclined to grant the anticipatory bail to the appellant.
Hence, the anticipatory bail is dismissed.
8. Accordingly, this appeal stands disposed of.
9. C.C. as per rules.
